**What I found**

The billing rules should move out of `src/orders/index.js` into a new `src/billing/index.js` module next to orders and shipping. Orders calls it while placing an order (the record calls this SPLIT, Proceed). The change history decided it. Over 26 weeks, 24 of the 31 commits that edit `src/orders/index.js` are finance rule changes (`FIN` tickets). None of them also carries an order ticket. Three of them broke the order lifecycle the next day: ORD-82 (orders stored without a status), ORD-85 (`placeOrder` returned the invoice instead of the order) and ORD-88 (orders stored without their lines).

**Why it matters**

After the move, a rule change edits only `src/billing/index.js`, which contains no order validation, storage or status code. That is the requirement's first done-when condition. The structural cost is one new module and one new import, which is the minimum any design meeting the requirement must add. If nothing changes, every weekly rule change keeps editing the function that validates and stores orders, and that edit caused 3 regressions in 26 weeks.

**Do this first**

1. Write the boundary rule before the code, in the same PR. It says `billing` may import nothing outside `billing`, and every file under `src/` must belong to a declared module. The repo has no linter, so this means adding ESLint and `eslint-plugin-boundaries` as dev dependencies plus an `npm run lint` script. Adding those dependencies is the team's decision.
   - Then create `src/billing/index.js` exporting `invoiceFor(country, lines)`. Move `TAX_BP`, `DISCOUNT_TIERS`, the unknown-country rejection with its exact message, and the invoice construction into it. In `placeOrder`, keep the empty-lines check first, then call `save({ customer, lines, status: "placed", invoice: invoiceFor(customer.country, lines) })`. JavaScript evaluates the arguments before `save` runs, so a rejected order is never stored. No test is needed to guarantee that.
   - Run `npm test` without changing any assertion, then `npm run lint`.

**What I did not check**

- Whether the tests pass. I made no edits and ran nothing, because this session can only read files. Run `npm test` before and after the change.
- Whether the change history is still current. This folder is not a git repository, so I couldn't confirm that `main` is still at `9c41e07`. Rerun the `git log` command at the top of `docs/evidence/change-history.md` in a real clone.
- Whether anything makes the tests and lint blocking. I found no CI configuration in the folder. Look in the real repo's pipeline config for a required step running `npm test` and `npm run lint`.
- The 50% threshold in the topology check was set after I had read the history. The result is the extreme case (every `FIN` commit is billing-only), so any threshold gives the same answer. The real test of the decision is the 13-week recheck after merge.
